paras: The killing of Tom Johnson was the fatal shooting of a Black man by Deputy Marshal Grant Cowan at Henryetta on or about 22 August 1905. It is known from a single sentence in the Guthrie Daily Leader, which gave no reason for the shooting.

According to the Guthrie Daily Leader of 23 August 1905, Deputy Marshal Grant Cowan "shot and killed Tom Johnson, colored, at Henryetta yesterday," which places the killing on 22 August. The item does not say what led to the shooting, whether Cowan was attempting an arrest, or whether Johnson was armed or accused of any offense.
No report of an inquest, arrest or further proceedings involving Cowan appears in the coverage.

The Guthrie Daily Leader ran the news as one line in its "Local Points" column, with no headline, placed among notes on baseball fans, the weather and local business. Johnson's race was given only as the identifier "colored," and the paper offered no comment on the killing. The same column, in a separate item, reported the killing of Joe Luster, "a negro," at Ardmore by "an unknown negro" during a quarrel.
No other white paper's report of the Henryetta shooting was found, and no Black-press coverage of it appears in the papers searched.
